thesis: Tetra Tech fell about 7.7% to $37.53 (from $40.65) in the regular session ahead of its fiscal Q4 report, which came after the close; the broker quote shows it trading around $41.10 after hours, which is not a confirmed regular-session reaction. The company-disclosed results (Business Wire, Nov 11): fourth-quarter revenue of $1.34B and net revenue of $1.15B (in line), adjusted EPS of $0.49 vs the $0.47 estimate; fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.60 on net revenue of $4.35B; backlog of $4.67B, up 13%; fiscal 2027 EPS guidance of $1.65-1.80; and a $500M increase to the share repurchase program. Counter-cases remain open: the December-quarter revenue guide of $1.04-1.08B is well below the fourth quarter's $1.34B, the 2025 loss of USAID work removed about $1.1B of backlog awards, and this run did not confirm how the fiscal 2027 guide compares with expectations. The Hunters Point False Claims Act matter was settled for $57M in Aug 2026 (private ancillary claims persist, with no scheduled ruling found; no restatement found). With the post-report reaction unconfirmed and these counter-cases unresolved, this is medium.
invalidation: Fiscal 2027 guidance is cut or backlog shrinks, or a close back below the pre-report close (~$37.53).
sources: AP via WTOP (fiscal Q4 earnings snapshot): https://wtop.com/national/2026/11/tetra-fiscal-q4-earnings-snapshot

thesis: Resideo rose about 18.1% to $22.98 (from $19.45) after its Nov 10 Q3 report (8-K), its first report since completing the ADI spin-off on Aug 3. Revenue was $727M, up 3% (up 6% excluding OEM Security); gross margin was 40.4%, the 14th straight quarter of year-over-year expansion; standalone adjusted EPS was $0.52, up 8%; and the full-year outlook was raised to revenue of $2.927-2.947B and standalone adjusted EBITDA of $614-624M, after the one-time $900M ADI dividend helped repay $1.1B of debt. Counter-cases remain open: the Q4 guide (EPS $0.42-0.48, revenue $710-730M) came in below consensus as OEM Security declines, and GAAP EPS from continuing operations was only $0.14. The litigation check found only a 2019 securities class action that settled for $55M, with no 2026 matter or restatement found. A confirmed, company-specific beat-and-raise with the Q4 shortfall unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: OEM Security declines spread to the rest of the business, the raised outlook is cut, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$19.45).
sources: Seeking Alpha (Q4 guide, OEM security declines): https://seekingalpha.com/news/4670357-resideo-forecasts-q4-2026-eps-of-0_42-0_48-and-revenue-of-710m-730m-as-oem-security-declines?feed_item_type=news

thesis: Payoneer was flat at $7.155 (prior close $7.16), $0.245 (about 3.4%) below the $7.40-per-share cash price Nuvei agreed to pay in June 2026 (about $2.75B equity value). The volume-spike and near-52-week-high signals reflect the stock trading as a pending cash takeover, not new company information: the deal is expected to close in mid-2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions, and a summary of the proxy materials mentions litigation and enhanced disclosures around the shareholder vote scheduled for Sept 14, 2026 (outcome not confirmed by this run; no scheduled ruling found). Upside is capped at the deal price, so the move is mechanical; low, avoid.
invalidation: The merger agreement is terminated or its terms change, so the stock trades on fundamentals again.

thesis: First Advantage was little changed at $21.55 (from $21.58) after a 3.7x-volume session on Nov 10 tied to Silver Lake's latest selling-stockholder offering: a Nov 9 free writing prospectus (Barclays and J.P. Morgan as underwriters) says Silver Lake will distribute up to 5.3M shares to its limited partners around closing, outside the lock-up. That follows Silver Lake's 12.5M-share sale at $22.20, which closed Aug 12; the company receives no proceeds. This run's searches did not surface a fundamental catalyst for the volume, which reflects sponsor share supply. The litigation check found a May 2026 plaintiff-firm data-breach investigation (no filed case found) and older FCRA class settlements that appear closed, with no restatement. A mechanical, supply-driven move makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: Sponsor selling ends and a company-disclosed result drives the shares.

thesis: Erasca rose about 8.5% to $16.79 (from $15.48) after crossing above its 200-day moving average, and this run found no company announcement explaining the move. Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman announced an investor investigation on Nov 11, and the securities class action Cheng v. Erasca (S.D. Cal., No. 26-cv-03481), over statements about ERAS-0015 Phase I data that included a patient death, remains pending with no scheduled ruling found. The shares also fell 9.95% to $13.39 on Oct 16 after a reported executive termination, which this run could not confirm in a company filing. A technical move with no company-specific catalyst makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: A company-disclosed clinical or business catalyst (e.g., new ERAS-0015 data) emerges that explains a re-rating.

thesis: Clorox edged up about 0.3% to $106.92 and is up about 19% over 60 days (from $89.31), with a 2.5x-volume session on Nov 10, but this run's searches found no company disclosure dated in November to explain the move. The latest items found are older: the April 30 fiscal Q3 report that cut the gross margin outlook on supply-chain costs and ERP stabilization (shares fell 9.67% the next day), a dividend increase to $1.25 on July 31, and the completed GOJO (Purell) acquisition. Pomerantz and Schall announced securities investigations in May 2026, with no filed complaint or restatement found. With no identified company-specific catalyst for the current move, this is low; avoid.
invalidation: A company disclosure (e.g., fiscal Q1 results showing margin recovery) identifies a fundamental driver for the rally.

thesis: Alcon fell about 2.2% to $72.45 (from $74.06), after trading at $70.91 (down 4.25%) early in the session, following its Nov 10 Q3 report: adjusted EPS beat but revenue missed, and full-year guidance was narrowed, with constant-currency sales growth now about 6% (from 5-7%) and core EPS growth 12-14% (from 12-15%). Intraocular lens sales fell 1% at constant currency on US competitive pressure, and a $58M one-off tariff refund helped operating income. The strongest counter-case is that the EPS beat and premium lens gains held up and the narrowed sales range keeps its midpoint; Needham kept a Buy rating, noting the guidance assumes the low end of 3% market growth, but that doesn't resolve the IOL share loss. The litigation check found 2026 consumer class actions over recalled Systane and GenTeal products (no ruling or settlement) and no restatement. A confirmed, company-specific negative print with an open counter-case makes this medium; avoid.
invalidation: IOL sales return to growth or guidance is raised at the next report.

thesis: Axogen rose about 15.2% to $58.63 (from $50.89), setting new 52-week highs, and this run's two searches found no company disclosure or other cause dated today. The company-specific catalyst on record is the Oct 28 Q3 report (8-K): revenue grew 26.2% to $75.8M, adjusted EBITDA rose to $13.4M from $9.2M, GAAP net income was $2.3M, and 2026 revenue guidance was raised to at least $290M (at least 29% growth, including at least $7M from BioCircuit). Counter-cases remain open: gross margin fell to 74.8% from 76.6%, the prostate nerve-reconstruction opportunity is excluded from guidance and not expected before 2027, and today's jump has no identified driver. The litigation check found only 2025 law-firm investigations tied to the FDA's extended Avance review (no filed case found) and an older derivative suit over 2017-2018 statements with no scheduled step found. A real earnings catalyst with an unexplained extension of the move makes this medium.
invalidation: Revenue growth slows against the raised guidance, gross margin keeps falling, or a close back below the pre-move level (~$50.89).

thesis: LifeStance slipped about 1.2% to $14.38 (from $14.56) after an 11.9M-share session on Nov 10 (2.1x average). The volume spike has no identified company catalyst: this run found no LifeStance news dated today, and its search surfaced only items on a selling-stockholder secondary offering's launch and pricing, which add share supply rather than fundamental news. The litigation check found the roughly $3.02M website-tracking privacy class settlement (Strong v. LifeStance, D. Ariz.), whose Oct 16, 2026 final approval hearing outcome wasn't found, and no restatement or 2026 investigation. A supply-driven move with no identified company catalyst makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: The offering supply clears and a company-disclosed result drives the shares.

thesis: SK Telecom's ADR rose about 3.8% to $34.355 (from $33.11) after a 2.1x-volume session on Nov 10; this run found no company news dated today. The company-specific catalyst is the Nov 4 Q3 report: revenue of KRW 4.4973T rose 13.1% year over year, operating income of KRW 552.3B topped KRW 500B for a third straight quarter, net income was KRW 411.8B versus a KRW 166.7B loss a year earlier, and the quarterly dividend held at KRW 830. Counter-cases remain open: the year-over-year jump is measured against the hacking-hit Q3 2025, handset subscribers declined, and breach-related exposure continues, including SK Telecom's suit to revoke the record KRW 134.8B privacy fine and consumer-agency compensation orders, with no scheduled ruling found. A confirmed earnings recovery with these counter-cases unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: Operating income falls back below KRW 500B, a breach ruling or compensation order materially raises costs, or a close back below the pre-move level (~$33.11).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV rose about 1.6% to $41.85, about 1.5% below its $42.50 52-week high, and this run's search found no company disclosure dated today. The latest company update found (quarter ended Sept 30, 2026) lists about $4.2B of cash and marketable securities, including a July payment from Moderna, reports that IMVT-1402 met its primary endpoint at the 600 mg dose in Period 2 of a late-line rheumatoid arthritis study, and sets an Investor Day for Dec 9. The thesis rests on the company's Nov 9 fiscal Q2 release cited in the prior thesis: LISRAYA (brepocitinib) generated $31.0M of net product revenue in its first five weeks after approval. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the non-infectious uveitis sNDA is not expected until 1H calendar 2027, so that indication is not yet approved. This stays medium.
invalidation: LISRAYA uptake stalls, or FDA feedback or full data reveal a uveitis safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).
sources: BiopharmaWatch (quarterly update, no Nov 11 items found): https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/ROIV/roivant-financial-results-q2-2026-business-update

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). Centene rose about 0.4% to $70.44, above the ~$68.03 pre-report level, and this run's search found no company disclosure dated today. Items found: CFO Drew Asher plans to step down in December 2026, with Chris Neczypor named successor effective Jan 1, 2027 (a planned transition with a named successor, not tied to execution problems in the reporting found); Centene has sued HHS and CMS over 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings it says will cost $448M, with no scheduled ruling found; and its 'Ohana Health Plan is leaving Hawaii's Medicaid program on Dec 31. The thesis rests on the company-specific Oct 27 Q3 report: EPS of $0.58, a consolidated HBR of 92.7%, and 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to at least $5.20. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: roughly $0.50 of non-recurring 2026 EPS, Medicaid membership declines and margin pressure, the 2027 Arkansas Medicaid expansion exit, and the Lunstrum v. Centene class action with no scheduled ruling. These cap this at medium.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).
sources: EarningsWhispers (Q3 2026 results and guidance, prior thesis source): https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/CNC/202609

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal; trimmed toward its low-conviction target on Nov 9). NWL slipped about 1.0% to $5.87, near the $5.82 cost, and this run's search found no new company disclosure (the latest items found date from mid-2026 or earlier; the quarterly dividend is $0.07). It remains above the ~$5.08 pre-report invalidation level. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open and keep the evidence mixed: the Oct 30 Q3 report cut the operating cash flow outlook about 62% to $150M, cited about $220M of inflation headwinds and a $101M impairment, and only maintained full-year adjusted EPS guidance. The early-exit window has passed (opened 6 trading days ago), but no new negative fact has emerged, so the direction stays long.
